newsitem.title: USA: Key senator scorns Clinton choice for Mexico envoy.
newsitem.headline: Key senator scorns Clinton choice for Mexico envoy.

text.p: Senate Foreign Relations committee chairman Jesse Helms scoffed on Tuesday at the Clinton administration's possible choice for U.S. ambassador to Mexico, Massachusetts Gov. William Weld, saying the White House ought to look for someone else.
Weld, a moderate Republican who has spoken in favour of abortion rights and the medical use of marijuana, had been sounded in May as a candidate for the Mexico ambassadorship.

"I don't think that he is ambassador quality and neither do a great many of the conservatives and Republicans in the state of Massachusetts," Helms, a North Carolina Republican, said in an interview with Fox News Channel.
"He's a little loose with his lips sometimes and that sort of thing. I have nothing against him, but I don't think he ought to be ambassador to Mexico," the veteran conservative senator added.
Helms acknowledged that he objected to Weld's views on the use of marijuana as medicine but declined to further criticise his fellow Republican.
Besides being a major transit point for cocaine smuggled into the United States, Mexico is also a big producer of heroin, methamphetamines and marijuana.

The Foreign Relations Committee must approve all ambassadorial appointees. Since he became chairman in 1994, Helms has wielded his authority to delay confirmation hearings to negotiate other pieces of legislation.
